title: River Review Execution Manifest
description: Content-addressed record of what River Review used to judge ONE review run (#2015, Epic #2011 Phase 4): the River Review version, plugin host, flow, agents, skills, input artifacts, policy, runtime and effective config. Produced by buildExecutionManifest (src/lib/execution-manifest.mjs) and verified by verifyExecutionManifest, which re-derives manifestKey / manifestId / manifestHash so a rewrite is detectable. NOT the Experiment Manifest: that document (schemas/paired-replay.schema.json, contract 3) pins a baseline/candidate EXPERIMENT over a dataset of already-produced runs, while this one pins a SINGLE run's execution configuration. This document records ids, versions and hashes only — hidden chain-of-thought, raw tool output and raw sensitive context are explicit non-goals, mechanically enforced by assertNoRawContext.

sha256.description: Bare lowercase hex sha256, or null when the source did not supply one. The `sha256:` prefix used by docs/data/skill-manifest.json is stripped by normalizeSha256 before it lands here.

status.description: Resolution status of one provenance block (#2015 AC 3). `resolved` means every field the block needs was supplied; `missing` means the source exists in this deployment but this run did not record it; `unavailable` means the caller explicitly declared there was nothing to pin (an empty skill selection, no agents). The distinction exists so that a null block is never read as a present one — that misreading is exactly how a run gets treated as replayable when it is not.

manifestId.description: Human-quotable id, derived from the first 12 hex characters of manifestKey. The RR-EXM- namespace is distinct from RR-PC- (promotion candidate) and RR-EXP- (experiment manifest).

manifestKey.description: sha256 over the manifest CONDITIONS only (createdAt and the derived ids excluded), so two runs under an identical execution configuration share a key and are directly comparable.

manifestHash.description: sha256 over the whole stored record including createdAt and the derived ids. This is the tamper check: any edit at all, the timestamp included, breaks it.

createdAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of manifest creation. Deliberately outside manifestKey.

reviewRunId.description: Canonical review_run_id of the run this manifest describes, resolved with deriveReviewRunId (src/lib/shadow-aggregate.mjs) — the contract-2 SSoT, never re-derived here.

host.description: Host that loaded the capability pack, e.g. "claude-code" or "codex".

flow.description: The flow definition this run executed (schemas/flow.schema.json, #2013). Flow INSTANCE documents now exist — #2016 landed flows/*.flow.json plus flows/entry-map.json — but src/lib/execution-manifest.mjs does not read them, because #2016 also pins an observe-mode guarantee that no module under src/ or runners/ loads that directory (tests/flow-definitions.test.mjs). The caller therefore passes the parsed document as `flowDocument` and `deriveFlowPin` hashes it (#2037); `sha256` is the digest of canonicalJson(document), not of the file bytes, so re-formatting the document does not invalidate the pin. A run that supplies no document leaves this block `missing`, which REPLAY_PINS treats as not replayable. The agent roster is the same shape: agents/contracts/*.agent.json (#2014) carry no checksum, so the caller hashes those too.

entries.description: Agent roster, sorted by id so the manifest hash does not depend on dispatch order.

status.description: `resolved` requires every selected skill to carry a sha256: an id alone cannot detect that the skill's text changed between run and replay, so an unchecksummed selection is a PARTIAL resolution and reports as `missing`.

skillSetHash.description: One digest over the sorted entries, so two runs' skill selections can be compared without walking the array.

entries.description: Input artifacts (requirements, diff, …) BY HASH ONLY. The contents are never copied here — that is what keeps a manifest from becoming a context dump.

riskMapDigest.description: The gate's risk-map digest (gate.inputs.riskMapDigest). It is a 16-hex TRUNCATION produced at src/lib/review-plan.mjs:842, not a sha256, so it keeps its own field — comparing two different lengths of the same hash would read as tampering.

sha256.description: Digest of the effective configuration. The config VALUES are never carried — a config can hold provider credentials.

redaction.description: Redaction applied to every string leaf before the digests were computed (#2015 AC 2). Recording the hit counts rather than the values keeps the manifest auditable without reproducing what was redacted.

writeEffects.description: Machine-checkable statement that building a manifest writes nothing. Always empty.
